meta.title: Cups of Tea Consumed in India per Week

prompt: How many cups of tea are consumed in all of India every week?

clarifications.answer: Only tea. Treat coffee and milk as separate.
Assume every day is identical for tea consumption.
Take India's population as about 1.45 billion.

common_traps: Applying one cups-per-person figure to the whole population without an age split, overcounting children.
Forgetting to multiply the daily figure by seven for a weekly answer.
Mixing units between crore and billion mid-calculation.

anchors.1: Multiplies total population by a single cups-per-person figure with no age reasoning.
anchors.3: Recognises age matters but applies a rough two-way split rather than proper age bands.
anchors.5: Uses an age-weighted demand approach rather than a single blanket per-capita rate.

anchors.1: No age split, or one that ignores that children barely drink tea.
anchors.3: Splits by age but assigns implausible per-band rates, e.g. children drinking as much as adults.
anchors.5: Splits by age bands with sensible per-band consumption, children near zero.

anchors.1: Unit chaos between crore and billion, or forgets to convert daily to weekly entirely.
anchors.3: Computes a daily figure correctly but slips on the times-seven or a unit conversion.
anchors.5: Keeps population and per-capita units consistent and multiplies by seven for the week.

anchors.1: No check on whether the per-capita rate is believable.
anchors.3: Notes a check is needed but doesn't compute the implied per-capita rate.
anchors.5: Checks that the implied per-capita rate (~0.9 cups/day) is believable for India.
